data.change_summary: Created baseline scenario envelope tests for all three shipped scenarios (nano_cycle, medium_planted, warm_room). Extended the Envelope type with 4 new assertion fields (algae_nuisance, biofilter_maturity, fast_stem_biomass_g, periphyton_biomass_g). Wrote 7 e2e tests exercising 500+ simulated hours each, with checkpoint envelope assertions covering cycling timeline, stable-state nutrients, DO behavior, shrimp mortality in uncycled tanks, thermal response, algae/plant competition, and cross-scenario relative behaviors. Each test includes detailed doc comments explaining what qualitative behavior the envelope protects and why those bounds exist. Also wrote diagnostic discovery tests for future baseline recalibration. Fixed pre-existing clippy lints in harness code.
outstanding_risks: Envelope bounds are intentionally wide to survive parameter tuning — they catch gross regressions but may not detect subtle behavioral changes. Downstream bead tanksim-6e5.7.3 should tighten these with literature-backed values.

All three baseline scenarios result in shrimp mortality (TAN too high in uncycled tanks). A 'well-maintained' scenario with properly seeded biofilter would be needed to exercise shrimp reproduction envelopes — this is deferred to tanksim-6e5.6.6.
The discover_baselines.rs test is a diagnostic tool that prints to stderr — it should be excluded from CI if output volume is a concern (no assertions, always passes).
Cross-scenario tests compare relative behaviors but don't assert absolute magnitudes — future phases should add quantitative cross-checks as the model matures.

steps.description: Explored codebase: scenario presets (nano_cycle, medium_planted, warm_room), existing test patterns, HarnessRun/Envelope API, tracing system, and budget infrastructure
Wrote discovery tests (discover_baselines.rs) to capture actual v0.1 simulation values at checkpoints for all three scenarios across 114 simulated days

Analyzed discovery output to identify key behavioral stories: pH crash in soft water, TAN accumulation killing shrimp, thermal equilibration, DO depression at warm temps, fast-stem vs rosette competition, algae growth patterns, biofilter maturation timeline
Extended Envelope struct with 4 new assertion fields (algae_nuisance, biofilter_maturity, fast_stem_biomass_g, periphyton_biomass_g) plus builder methods and check logic in tank_harness/src/lib.rs
Wrote nano_cycle_baseline_envelope test: 2736 hours, fishless cycle showing pH crash + TAN accumulation, shrimp mortality, plant decline in soft water
Wrote medium_planted_baseline_envelope test: 2736 hours, active substrate nutrients, guild competition (fast stems dominate rosettes), biofilter maturation, rising algae pressure
Wrote warm_room_baseline_envelope test: 2736 hours, thermal equilibration to 29C, reduced DO saturation, accelerated algae growth, thermal stress on shrimp
Wrote cross_scenario_relative_behaviors test: verifies warm_room is warmer with lower DO saturation, medium_planted has more plant biomass than others
Wrote thermal_inertia_scales_with_tank_size test: nano (30L) equilibrates faster than medium (65L) to ambient temperature change
Wrote do_dips_at_night_in_planted_tank test: dark-period DO mean <= lit-period DO mean due to respiration without photosynthesis
Wrote biofilter_matures_during_cycling test: all three scenarios show biofilter maturity increase > 0.2 over 30 days of feeding
Fixed pre-existing clippy lints: moved #[cfg(test)] mod to end of lib.rs, fixed len_zero in e2e_nano_neglect.rs, fixed SubstrateKind field init in tank_scenarios
Ran full test suite (all workspace crates): all tests pass. Ran cargo clippy -- -D warnings: clean. Ran cargo fmt --check: clean.

validation_evidence: cargo test (full workspace): all tests pass including 7 new e2e_baseline_scenarios tests, 3 discover_baselines tests, and all pre-existing tests
cargo clippy --package tank_harness --tests -- -D warnings: zero warnings/errors (including test-only clippy lints)
All 7 baseline tests exercise 500+ simulated hours (2736+ hours = 114 days each) with structured envelope assertions at multiple checkpoints
Each baseline test produces CI-friendly exit codes (0 = pass, non-zero = envelope violation) and supports TANK_E2E_VERBOSE=1 for full trace dumps
Envelope bounds are scientifically motivated with doc-comment explanations of 'what should happen and why' for each constraint
